KC's recent identity is Kenneth Walker (55 carries, 341 rush yards over weeks 4/6/7) into a DEN front allowing 4.72 YPC and 26 runs of 10+. DEN's identity is an inefficient committee run game (J.K. Dobbins 41/132, 3.2 YPC) plus vertical shots that are not converting (Jaylen Waddle 19 targets, 176 air yards, only 91 rec yards) against a KC defense allowing 3.60 YPC and 16 passes of 20+ on 218 attempts.
script.flip1: DEN gets up early at home, the line-move script. KC chases through the air, Walker carries fall out of the high teens and the rush-over dies, and Waddle's target count rises enough that one connecting shot can beat 39.5. Dobbins can keep handing off but KC's 3.60 YPC still caps him.
script.flip2: Walker rips early explosives (DEN has allowed 26 runs of 10+ in 7 games), KC leads and clocks it. DEN abandons the run, Bo Nix drops back into his -0.19 EPA blitz split, checkdowns replace Waddle air yards, and both the Walker over and the Waddle under cash together.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Walker is the entire KC run game (55 carries, 341 yards over the last 3) and DEN is bleeding exactly that (4.72 YPC, 26 runs of 10+ in 7 games), so in a one-score game he is the offense's top option attacking the defense's weak spot. Script-dependent: dies if KC trails big.
edge_players.must_be_true: He plays a full workload near 16-18 carries, no inactive or snap cap, and the game stays competitive or KC leads so Andy Reid does not abandon the run. DEN does not sell out to a stacked box the whole night.
edge_players.kills_it: Flip 1: DEN leads by two scores early, KC throws to chase, carries drop into the low teens, and 14 carries at even 5.0 YPC finishes near 70. A late Walker scratch or a Johnson/Mahomes vulture on the only explosives also kills it.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Waddle is DEN's primary receiver but the shots are not cashing: 19 targets, 176 air yards, only 91 rec yards (30.3/game, 4.8 yards/target) over weeks 5-7, and KC allows just 16 passes of 20+ on 218 attempts with a strong right side (4.83 YPA), so 39.5 sits above both the role and the explosives environment.
edge_players.must_be_true: He stays the vertical WR1 rather than a sudden short-area hog, Nix does not suddenly connect downfield, and the game does not turn into a shootout. KC's 27% blitz rate is enough, with Nix at -0.19 EPA vs blitz, to keep some of those air yards as checkdowns to Engram/Harvey instead.
edge_players.kills_it: One 40-plus yard play against KC's softer left or middle (7.26 and 8.02 YPA), or DEN trailing and feeding him 10-plus targets in a shootout. A late Waddle inactive would void the leg, and inactives are not in the pack.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost because DEN led 17-3 at half, KC abandoned Walker after 11 carries for 48, and the rush over never had a fourth-quarter chance, while Waddle caught a 46-yard corner against KC's left side (7.26 YPA) on one play-action shot and finished 4-52 to beat 39.5 on a single explosive the 16-of-218 rate said was unlikely but not impossible. The other way the card dies is the unresolved injury board: if Dobbins was actually limited and the game script flipped to a DEN pass-heavy chase, both the Walker carry assumption and the Waddle efficiency assumption were the wrong story, and the Oct 29 checklist already warned that Thursday reports and inactives were still pending.
slip_story: One story only: divisional grind at altitude, not a shootout. KC runs through Walker in a one-score or KC-lead script (flip 2 and the base case), and DEN's downfield air yards to Waddle do not convert against a KC defense that stuffs explosives. Do not pair this with a game over, a Worthy/Kelce over, or a Coleman role-change over; those need the opposite script or an unconfirmed injury. Two legs, no TDs. Walker is script-dependent on flip 1 (DEN up big).
